$comment: The gate commands for agent-mpc-voice-control-1. kaliper:phased-implement reads this file and never invents a command: an empty array or a null means UNCONFIGURED, and the skill reports that gate as NOT RUN rather than guessing. Filled by hand at T006 — every command below was executed and observed green before being written here, per the rule that a gate running an inferred command reports PASS and means nothing. Nothing replaces this file without --redetect-gates. `npm run test:e2e:live` (added at T093) needs network, YOUTUBE_API_KEY and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in dev.env, and spends real quota and assistant turns; it is the only gate that exercises the real embed and the real assistant, so a missing prerequisite is reported NOT RUN, never skipped as passing.

fast.why: Cheapest and catches the most. Runs first so a type error stops the phase before a slower suite spends time on it.
Vitest, contract and integration only. The e2e suite is excluded by the include globs in vite.config.ts and belongs in `final`, because it needs browser binaries and a running server.
Last of the fast gate: it is the slowest, and a type or unit failure makes it redundant.

live.note: Port 5273 is deliberate, not the Vite default. A test-agent-mcp dev server occupies 5173 on this machine, and an e2e run attached to it and asserted against that unrelated app's DOM. vite.config.ts sets strictPort so a collision fails loudly instead of drifting to the next free port while the runner talks to whatever holds 5273; playwright.config.ts sets reuseExistingServer:false for the same reason. Readiness: the Vite dev server answers within about a second, but a rendered shell is not a working feature — once the backend exists, check that the ticket endpoint answers before treating a connected-looking UI as ready. Since T092 the live start runs the backend and Vite as one process group; if either dies both stop, so a half-running stack cannot pass for a working one.
